newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open weaker after rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open weaker after rate cut.

text.p: Australian shares opened weaker on Wednesday as investors took profits following a long-awaited decision by the Reserve Bank to cut official interest rates.
At 10.25 a.m. (2325 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 11 points weaker at 2,350.6.
Blue chip stocks started weaker across the board with all the major banks drifting lower.
However, most selling was concentrated on major resource issues, including BHP and CRA, after base and precious metal prices sagged on Tuesday.
"I can't remember a rate cut that was more in the market than this one," said Eric Gale, director of institutions at Sydney brokerage Ord Minnett.
Gale said the local equity market had been expecting the 50 basis point cut but it was possible that the local bond market may have been expecting slightly more.
"The market got what it expected and I think investors are now taking profits," he said.
Dealers said that despite the rate easing, turnover remained subdued after the Melbourne Cup holiday which saw the Melbourne market closed and sidelined many other investors on Tuesday.
